neighbours.label: Concessive 'but' and similar clause links in prose that explains software design or code ('not strictly necessary, but ...'), vs the same links in prose about everyday topics
fire: This wrapper class is not really required, but it makes the API easier to mock.
The cache layer is optional, but it speeds up repeated queries a lot.
This helper function is not strictly needed, but it keeps the parser readable.
The config loader could read the file directly, but we validate it first.
The retry decorator is not essential, but it hides flaky network errors.
This interface adds some boilerplate, but it lets plugins share one contract.
The logging module is not mandatory here, but it helps when debugging crashes.
The adapter is a thin layer, but it isolates the database driver from the rest.
quiet: This winter coat is not really required, but it makes the walk more pleasant.
The dessert course is optional, but most guests stay for it.
This umbrella is not strictly needed, but it keeps the rain off your bag.
The bakery could close early, but it stays open for regulars.
The second alarm clock is not essential, but it helps on Mondays.
This old sofa takes up some space, but it lets three people sit together.
The guidebook is not mandatory here, but it helps when visiting museums.
The fence is a low barrier, but it keeps the dog out of the garden.

predictions: Code-explanation sentences reach 0.2-0.5 on 'but'; everyday-topic versions stay under 0.1.
notes: Card: This, Additionally, but, is, can in code comments and docstrings. Probe: 'This module is not strictly necessary, but' 0.476, '# Additionally, we shuffle' 0.285; the weather version 'not strictly pleasant, but' 0.071, prose 'Additionally' 0.109, '# This function iterates' only 0.051.
